newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares reverse gains, choppy trade seen.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares reverse gains, choppy trade seen.

text.p: Shares at Bombay exchanges retreated from an early mid-morning rally on Tuesday as profit-takers lurked following yesterday's blistering uptrend, traders said.
The market undertone however remained upbeat with players expecting a breather before the next upward charge.

"Interest is shifting to many stocks," said Kirti Doshi, a dealer at Biyani Securities. "There is continued enquiries by foreign funds in many stocks and on the supply side also, major local funds are quiet."

By 1120 a.m. (0550 GMT), Bombay's benchmark 30-share was up 4.22 points at 4,260.31, off 4,288.75 -- the day's early high. The blue chip gauge on Monday staged a three percent rally on the back of a sharp rise in index-heavyweight stocks.
"The market looks nice. The rally should now start percolating to the second-liner stocks," said Sanjay Vaid, chief dealer at Lloyds Securities.
"There was a good amount of foreign fund buying yesterday. We seem to be in a decent bull market."
The market's sharp gains are unlikely to attract profit-taking in a big way, though a minor technical correction is expected at higher levels, traders said.
"In a run-away market, nobody is prepared to book profits," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage.
Cement stocks continue to climb higher on the changing market outlook for the sector as analysts said cheaper valuations lured buyers.
Associated Cement Companies (ACC) rose 46.50 rupees to 1,499.0, and Gujarat Ambuja Cement gained 2.50 rupees to 349.0, another 52-week high.
Early indications of higher price realisations and better volumes in the first few months of the year have propelled cement stocks into favour, traders said.
Among other individual stocks, power generator and supplier BSES Ltd rose 1.50 rupees to 239.75, before jumping to 244.0.
The firm announced a rise in its 1996/97 (April-March) net profit to 2.13 billion rupees from 1.73 billion last year.
The company stepped up dividend to 3.0 rupees per share from 2.80 the previous year.
